headline: UN ends its Western Sahara mission after 35 years

sources.title: UN's peacekeeping mission in disputed Western Sahara ends after 35 years (NPR)
UN warns of security risks in Western Sahara as peacekeeping mission ends (Al Jazeera)
As peacekeepers leave Western Sahara, refugees yearn to end a half-century wait (Reuters via Al-Monitor)

chunks.text: On November 1, 2026, the United Nations {{shut down}} its [[peacekeeping mission]] in Western Sahara after 35 years. Western Sahara is a [[desert territory]] on Africa's northwestern coast. The UN {{set up}} the mission in 1991. Its [[troops]] were there to [[monitor]] a [[cease-fire]], an agreement to stop fighting.

verbs.wrong: To give an operation a new leader

chunks.text: Morocco and the Polisario Front, an [[independence movement]] backed by Algeria, both [[claim]] the territory. Morocco {{took over}} in 1975, when Spain, the territory's old ruler, left. Morocco now runs nearly all of it. The movement wants an [[independent state]] there. A war {{broke out}} between the two sides and lasted over 15 years. More than 16,000 people died, according to the French Senate. Thousands fled and {{ended up}} in [[refugee camps]] in Algeria.

verbs.why: In this board game, players take over one country at a time. A big company takes over the town's only airport. Morocco took over the territory in 1975, when Spain left.

verbs.wrong: To be reported in the newspapers
verbs.why: Fights often break out at the end of hockey games. Arguments break out when the two families meet. A war broke out over Western Sahara and lasted more than 15 years.

verbs.correct: To finally be in a place
verbs.wrong: To cross a border at night
verbs.why: Lost bags often end up at the wrong airport. Many students end up in a big city after college. Thousands of people fled the war and ended up in camps in Algeria.

chunks.text: The UN also planned a [[referendum]], a [[public vote]] on the territory's future. That vote {{fell through}} because the two sides disagreed about who could vote. The conflict has {{dragged on}} for about 50 years. The movement {{pulled out}} of the cease-fire in 2020. The [[dispute]] {{heated up}} in 2025, when the UN's main peace body, the Security Council, supported Morocco's plan to give the territory [[self-rule]] under Moroccan control. On October 30, 2026, Russia stopped a U.S. plan backing that idea. Five council members, including Russia, have a [[veto]], the power to block decisions.

verbs.why: Many house sales fall through when the bank says no. Travel plans often fall through when someone gets sick. The vote on the territory's future fell through because the two sides disagreed about who could vote.

A company often pulls out when a deal costs too much. Some countries pull out of a trade agreement after an election. The Polisario Front pulled out of the cease-fire in 2020.

verbs.wrong: To get the attention of a court
verbs.why: The fight over the new school heats up every spring. The debate about parking heats up when the city raises prices. The dispute heated up in 2025, when the Security Council supported Morocco's plan.

chunks.text: Eleven of the 15 members supported the U.S. plan. The U.S. said its plan would have brought progress, but Russia said the plan favored one side. The council {{voted down}} a Russian plan to extend the mission, so its [[mandate]], or [[official permission]] to operate, {{ran out}}. Morocco's [[royal palace]] welcomed the result. The Polisario Front called it unacceptable, and Algeria blamed U.S. [[bias]]. The UN's leader warned of a risk of more fighting and {{called on}} all sides to stay calm.

verbs.wrong: To count the votes a second time
verbs.why: Workers often vote down a bad contract. The city council votes down most plans for new parking. The Security Council voted down a Russian plan to extend the mission.

verbs.why: My parking permit runs out at the end of the month. Most passports run out after ten years. The mission's mandate ran out when the council could not agree.

verbs.wrong: To thank someone in public for their work
verbs.why: Parents call on the school to make lunch healthier. Doctors call on people to get more sleep. The UN's leader called on all sides to stay calm.

mainIdea.s: A long UN peacekeeping effort in Western Sahara has ended after Russia and the U.S. could not agree on the territory's future. The promised vote never happened, and many refugees remain in Algeria.
mainIdea.why: The mandate ran out after a Russian veto and a failed Russian plan. The referendum fell through, and families who fled ended up in camps in Algeria.

mainIdea.s: Soldiers left the desert region because the fighting was over and both sides asked them to go. Now that peace has come, families living in camps can plan their trip home after fifty years away.
mainIdea.why: Close, but no peace deal ended the mission. The mandate ran out because of a fight at the Security Council, and the UN warned of a risk of more fighting.

mainIdea.s: Spain has agreed to pay for new schools and clean water systems across North Africa. Officials in Madrid say the work should start next spring, and it could take about four years to finish.
mainIdea.why: This story is about the end of a UN mission. The UN shut down its peacekeeping work in Western Sahara after a fight at the Security Council.

lines.text: Did you see that the UN {{shut down}} its mission in Western Sahara?
I saw that. Where exactly is Western Sahara?
On Africa's northwestern coast. It's mostly desert.
And who does it belong to?
[[It's complicated]]. Spain left in 1975, and Morocco {{took over}}.
Did anyone try to stop that?
Yes. A war {{broke out}} with the Polisario Front, which wants independence.
So when did the peacekeepers arrive?
The UN {{set up}} the mission in 1991. It was supposed to organize a vote, too.
It {{fell through}}. The two sides couldn't agree on who could vote.
So this has {{dragged on}} for about 50 years. Why did the mission end now?
Russia vetoed a U.S. plan. It said the council shouldn't [[take sides]].
And then the council {{voted down}} Russia's plan?
So are they [[back to square one]]?
Maybe. [[There's no telling]] what happens next. The UN {{called on}} everyone to stay calm.
I keep thinking about the families. They {{ended up}} [[in limbo]] in those camps.
